question: Why can water stay liquid at −10 °C, then freeze the moment you tap it?
answer: Purified water can stay liquid below 0 °C, as the bottle at −10 °C does, and it freezes when tapped. Freezing gives off heat, so only part of the water turns to ice, about 1/80 per degree, and the rest sits at 0 °C.
move: Freezing gives off heat, so supercooled water turns only part to ice, about 1/80 per degree, then sits at 0 °C.
